item.description: The Sustainable Development Goals aim to improve lives, but it is unclear whether progress on Sustainable Development Goal indicators translates into greater subjective well-being over time. A study of 42 countries found associations in levels, but weak links with year-to-year changes in life evaluations.

item.title: 【環境】 On living and feeling better
item.description: As the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) enter their final years, there is a desire to reflect on their societal impact. A study now compares changes in the SDG indicators with changes in how people feel about their lives and finds no detectable correlation between the two.

item.title: 【AI4S】 Filter By:
item.description: Minority and underserved youth are less likely to undergo diabetic retinopathy screening, yet more likely to have diabetic retinopathy. We hypothesize that autonomous artificial intelligence-based diabetic eye exams could mitigate screening disparities in minority youth. This prospective study enrolled 397 White and non-White youth with type 1 (72%) and type 2 (28%) diabetes at diabetes care visits. Participants underwent autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exams and optical coherence tomography imaging. The primary outcome is equivalence in screening completion between White and non-White youth. The secondary outcome is diagnostic accuracy of AI against prognostic standard. At baseline, participants in the White cohort were more likely to have completed a prior diabetic eye exam (79.8% v 61.8%, p < 0.0001). Following the artificial-intelligence intervention, 99.5% in the White cohort and 98% in the non-White cohort completed the autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exam, demonstrating equivalent screening completion after implementation.
